answer: Require every new identity to lock a refundable bond that is slashed when its attestations are overturned, and let its weight grow only through weeks of verified, paid work. Reputation then behaves like pigment bound in paint: it fixes slowly and cannot be washed off and reused for a fresh clone. Cross-audits act as a gale and a falcon together, scattering cheap copies and spotting linked wallets, so each fake identity must risk fresh capital and real computation, costing an attacker nearly as much as running one honest agent.
